$comment: Phase 2 integration ledger. Every entry is something this suite CANNOT verify
in-process, together with the observable condition that will make it verifiable.
The enforcing test (test_integration_ledger.py) fails in BOTH directions:
- an entry whose precondition is now satisfied must be promoted to a real test
and removed from here (otherwise the ledger is a place coverage goes to die);
- an entry whose precondition regressed is a broken dependency.
It is deliberately not a skip list. pytest.mark.skip is invisible in a green run,
and invisible non-coverage is the failure mode this whole plan exists to catch.

PROMOTED 2026-09-04: 'ci-runs-any-of-this' is gone. A workflow now exists (.github/workflows/build-and-test.yml) and this suite runs in it, so the entry's premise was false and the ledger fails it deliberately. Coverage moved to tests/production/test_ci_runs_this_suite.py. Everything still listed below is blocked on something that does not exist in this environment, not on someone not having written it.

entries.claim: A persisted trace survives process restart and replays identically from Cosmos.
entries.why_pending: COSMOS_DB_ENDPOINT is unset in this environment, so the service falls back to an in-memory sink. Replay fidelity is proven against that sink, which is the same object the live stream reads — durability across processes is NOT proven.
entries.promote_when: A Cosmos emulator or a deployed account is reachable from the test environment.

entries.claim: The copilot identity can read its containers and cannot write copilot-approvals.
entries.why_pending: Terraform is asserted as text. The actual RBAC grant is only observable against a deployed subscription.
entries.promote_when: terraform plan/apply runs against a real subscription in CI.

entries.claim: propose_action creates an approval in status 'proposed' in the real authority-service and cannot advance it.
entries.why_pending: authority-service is a separate .NET process, not running here. The transport is proven with a recording double; the far end is not.
entries.promote_when: docker compose or the local stack can bring both services up in the test job.

entries.claim: A real model in the agent loop cannot name a write tool, because none is offered to it.
entries.why_pending: No Foundry endpoint is configured; the loop under test is the scripted one. The tool LIST offered to the model is proven; the model's behaviour when given adversarial input is not.
entries.promote_when: An evaluation environment with a model endpoint exists (#333).
entries.would_be_covered_by: the eval harness, not this suite

entries.claim: nginx does not buffer /api/copilot/ in a running stack.
entries.why_pending: The config is asserted as text. A running nginx is what proves it.
entries.promote_when: The local stack is started as part of the test job.

entries.claim: The /copilot page renders the stream, the evidence pane and the approval card from real frames.
entries.why_pending: Playwright e2e needs both the UI dev server and the service. This suite is Python-side only.
entries.promote_when: tests/e2e gains a copilot spec and the stack runs in CI.
